popular.what: Park headquarters and a short climb to a sunset viewpoint.

popular.name: Koh Adang
popular.what: Jungle island next to Lipe with the Chado Cliff viewpoint and Pirate Falls.

popular.name: Ao Son
popular.what: A long, wild beach on Tarutao's west coast where turtles nest.

gems.name: Crocodile Cave (Tham Jorakhe)
gems.what: A longtail ride up a mangrove river to a limestone cave.

gems.name: Ao Taloh Wao
gems.what: The old prison camp site on the east coast, with ruins and a small museum.

localFavs.name: Park canteen
localFavs.what: Simple Thai food at Ao Pante and Laem Son.

localFavs.name: Roti
localFavs.what: Southern Thai and Malay roti from Lipe's stalls.

crowd.quietest: Any weekday on Koh Tarutao; Adang is quietest before 9 am.
crowd.busiest: Christmas to February on Koh Adang trails, with Lipe day trippers.
crowd.note: Park accommodation closes from about mid-May to mid-October.

basics: Thai baht (THB). Cards work in cities and malls; carry cash for markets, street food and islands. ATMs charge a fixed fee per withdrawal, so take out more at once.
Grab and Bolt for rides in cities; overnight trains and buses between regions; cheap domestic flights; ferries and longtail boats to the islands.

Cool and dry Nov to Feb in most of the country. The Andaman coast (Phuket, Krabi, Phi Phi, Lanta) is best Nov to Apr; the Gulf islands (Samui, Tao) are often best Jan to Aug. The north can be smoky in March and April.
Cover shoulders and knees, take shoes off where others do, never point your feet at a Buddha, and don't touch monks if you are a woman.
The monarchy is deeply respected and protected by strict laws: never joke about or criticise the royal family. Stand for the royal anthem in cinemas.
Buy a tourist SIM or eSIM at the airport. Plugs are mostly types A, B, C and O, at 230 V.
Philippine passport holders can visit Thailand visa-free for a limited stay. Check the current allowed length of stay and the Thailand Digital Arrival Card requirement before you fly.

cities.name: Bangkok
cities.getAround: BTS and MRT rides cost about 17 to 65 baht, river boats 16 to 30 baht and the Tha Tien cross-river ferry about 5 baht. Grab or Bolt across the centre is usually 80 to 250 baht; agree tuk-tuk prices first (100 to 200 baht for short hops).

timing.avoid: Apr to May: hottest weeks, often above 35 C. Sep to Oct: heaviest rain and some street flooding.
timing.note: Songkran water fights in mid April; Loy Krathong lanterns on the river in November.

vibe.line: Loud, hot, delicious and nonstop: temples by day, rooftops and street woks by night.

eat.name: Nai Ek Roll Noodles, Yaowarat
eat.what: Peppery rolled-noodle soup with crispy pork; a Chinatown late-night classic.

eat.name: Or Tor Kor Market
eat.what: Cleanest fresh market in town: mango sticky rice, curries, top-grade fruit.

eat.name: Krua Apsorn
eat.what: Crab omelette and stir-fried crab in yellow curry; homestyle Thai, fair prices.

do.name: Orange-flag river boat from Sathorn
do.what: Same river views as the tourist boat for a fraction; hop off at Tha Tien.

do.name: Bang Krachao bike loop
do.what: Rent a bike across the river: jungle paths, raised walkways, weekend floating market.

do.name: Muay Thai at Rajadamnern Stadium
do.what: Real fight night with local gamblers yelling; upper seats are cheapest.

night.name: Jodd Fairs Ratchada
night.what: Night market: grilled seafood, giant spicy pork ribs, cheap beer, big crowd.

night.name: Tep Bar, Chinatown
night.what: Chill bar with live traditional Thai music and Thai-herb cocktails.

night.name: Soi Rambuttri and Khao San
night.what: Party: buckets, loud bars, street dancing; Rambuttri is calmer and cheaper.

know: Take the orange-flag boat at about 16 baht flat; the blue tourist boat charges several times more for the same route.
A tuk-tuk offering a 20 baht tour ends at gem or suit shops. Smile, walk away, book Grab.
Many Chinatown and Old Town stalls close on Mondays for street cleaning; save your food crawl for another night.

cities.name: Ayutthaya
cities.getAround: Bicycles rent for about 50 to 100 baht a day and scooters 200 to 300. A tuk-tuk for a few hours around the ruins is roughly 300 to 500 baht per vehicle (agree the route first).

timing.avoid: Mar to May: very hot with little shade at the ruins. Sep to Oct: river flooding is possible.
timing.note: Day-trippers peak 10 am to 2 pm; stay overnight to see the ruins lit up in the evening.

vibe.line: Sleepy river island of crumbling red-brick temples, best explored slowly by bike.

eat.name: Roti sai mai stalls, U Thong Road
eat.what: Ayutthaya’s candy-floss roti: buy a pack fresh, roll your own.

eat.name: Chao Phrom Market
eat.what: Local market by the river: boat noodles, grilled pork, fruit for pennies.

eat.name: Malakor
eat.what: Thai classics in a wooden house facing Wat Ratchaburana; great after temple hopping.

do.name: Cycle the island
do.what: Temples are flat and close together; a bike is cheaper and freer than a tuk-tuk.

do.name: Sunset longtail around the island
do.what: Boat circles past riverside temples as the light turns gold.

do.name: Bang Pa-In Palace
do.what: Royal summer palace with lakes and pavilions, 20 minutes south.

night.name: Hua Ro night market
night.what: Night market: cheap noodles, grilled skewers, Thai families out for dinner.

night.name: Lit-up Wat Mahathat
night.what: Quiet stroll: some ruins are floodlit after dark, free to view from outside.

night.name: Soi Farang bars, Naresuan Road
night.what: Chill backpacker bars, cheap Leo and pool tables; small but friendly.

know: Rent a bike for 50 to 100 baht a day; tuk-tuk temple tours run about 200 to 300 baht per hour.
The ordinary train from Bangkok costs around 15 to 20 baht in third class and beats tour vans.
Start by 8 am: by noon the brick ruins radiate heat and day-trip coaches roll in from Bangkok.

cities.name: Kanchanaburi
cities.getAround: Bus 8170 runs from town to Erawan for about 50 to 60 baht each way, about 1.5 hours. Scooters rent for 200 to 300 baht a day; songthaews and motorbike taxis cover short hops for 30 to 60 baht.

timing.avoid: Mar to May: hot, and the falls run lower. Sep to Oct: muddy trails and murkier pools.
timing.note: River Kwai Bridge Week in late Nov to early Dec brings a light and sound show and big crowds.

vibe.line: River rafthouses, jungle waterfalls and sobering war history, all in slow motion.

eat.name: Saeng Chuto Road stalls
eat.what: Pad krapao and khao man gai for office-worker prices.

eat.name: Kanchanaburi night market by the station
eat.what: Grilled fish, som tam and desserts; locals outnumber tourists.

eat.name: Keeree Tara
eat.what: Riverside terrace near the bridge: river fish, spicy salads, sunset views.

do.name: Death Railway train to Nam Tok
do.what: Creaky train over the Wang Pho wooden viaduct, cliffs on one side.

do.name: Hellfire Pass memorial walk
do.what: Moving trail through the rock cutting; museum is excellent, entry by donation.

do.name: Kayak or bamboo raft the River Kwai
do.what: Lazy paddle past rafthouses and limestone hills.

night.name: Mae Nam Khwae Road bars
night.what: Chill bars and live acoustic sets along the backpacker strip.

night.name: River Kwai Bridge at dusk
night.what: Sunset spot: walk the bridge as lamps come on, then grab street snacks.

know: Stay on Mae Nam Khwae Road: rafthouse rooms run about 400 to 900 baht, scooters 200 to 250 a day.
Public bus to Erawan Falls costs about 50 to 60 baht; check the last return, usually mid-afternoon.
Foreigners pay 100 baht for the Death Railway; sit on the river side for the viaduct views.

cities.name: Sukhothai
cities.getAround: Blue songthaews run between New Sukhothai and the old city for about 30 to 40 baht, 30 minutes. Bicycles at the park gates rent for about 30 to 50 baht a day.

timing.avoid: Mar to May: very hot for cycling the ruins. Aug to Oct: heavy rain.
timing.note: Loy Krathong (November) is celebrated here with a week of lights and lanterns: book rooms early.

vibe.line: Calm, golden and green: lotus ponds, giant Buddhas and early-morning bike rides.

eat.name: Noodle stalls by the Old City gate
eat.what: Sukhothai noodles: sweet-sour pork broth, peanuts, green beans.

eat.name: New Town night market
eat.what: Locals’ dinner: grilled chicken, sticky rice, fruit shakes.

eat.name: Jay Hae
eat.what: Famous Sukhothai noodle shop; order the dry version and a coconut jelly.

do.name: Dawn bike ride to the west zone
do.what: Empty forest temples and a hilltop Buddha before the heat.

do.name: Si Satchanalai Historical Park
do.what: Sukhothai’s quieter twin, an hour north; often you have it to yourself.

do.name: Sangkhalok Museum
do.what: Small private museum of old Sukhothai ceramics; cool break from the sun.

night.name: Chopper Bar, New Town
night.what: Chill rooftop bar with live music and cheap Thai plates.

night.name: Old City sunset by the ponds
night.what: Quiet sunset spot: ruins reflected in lotus ponds, then fireflies and frogs.

know: Sleep in the Old City, not New Town, so you can cycle the ruins at 6:30 am.
Blue songthaews link New Town and the Old City for about 30 baht; last ones leave late afternoon.
Loy Krathong here is Thailand’s most famous; rooms double in price, so book weeks ahead.

cities.name: Chiang Mai
cities.getAround: Red songthaews are shared taxis: about 30 to 50 baht within town if you share, more to go further. Grab or Bolt is 60 to 200 baht across town; scooters rent for 200 to 350 baht a day.

timing.avoid: Mar to Apr: burning season smoke and haze, poor air quality. Jun to Sep: rainy.
timing.note: Yi Peng lanterns and Loy Krathong in November draw huge crowds; Songkran in April is the wettest party in the country.

vibe.line: Laid-back mountain city of cafes, khao soi, temples and the cheapest massages around.

eat.name: Chang Phueak Gate night stalls
eat.what: Braised pork leg on rice from the cowboy-hat lady, plus smoothies.

eat.name: Warorot Market
eat.what: Northern snacks: sai oua sausage, nam prik dips, crispy pork to take away.

eat.name: Huen Phen
eat.what: Northern Thai in an antique-filled house: khao soi, gaeng hang lay.

do.name: Cooking class with market tour
do.what: Half-day class, five dishes, farm or market visit; most include pickup.

do.name: Sticky Waterfall (Bua Tong)
do.what: Climb up a waterfall with grippy limestone; free and fun.

do.name: Wat Umong forest temple
do.what: Tunnel temple in the woods, quiet monks, feed the fish.

night.name: Sunday Walking Street
night.what: Huge night market down Ratchadamnoen: crafts, food, temple-yard dining.

night.name: North Gate Jazz Co-op
night.what: Live music: packed jam sessions spilling onto the street.

night.name: Nimman Soi 11 and Think Park
night.what: Party-lite: student bars, craft beer, small clubs nearby.

know: Red songthaews are shared: say your stop, pay about 30 to 40 baht in town; agree before boarding.
February to April is smoke season; check AQI and plan Pai or the islands instead if it’s bad.
Local massage shops charge about 200 to 300 baht an hour, half of Bangkok spa prices.

cities.name: Pai
cities.getAround: Pai is small: walk the town, then rent a scooter (150 to 250 baht a day) for canyon, falls and hot springs. Without a licence and experience, hire a local driver or join a sightseeing tour (about 300 to 500 baht).

timing.avoid: Mar to Apr: smoky and hazy. Jul to Sep: slippery mountain road and landslide risk.
timing.note: Dec to Jan weekends fill with Thai holidaymakers; book ahead and pack a warm layer for nights near 10 C.

vibe.line: Hippie mountain valley: scooters, sunsets, hot springs and bars that start late.

eat.name: Pai Walking Street stalls
eat.what: Khao soi, lasagne, mango sticky rice, anything on a stick.

eat.name: Pai Morning Market
eat.what: Local breakfast: jok rice porridge, patongo, fresh soy milk.

eat.name: Om Garden Cafe
eat.what: Healthy brunch bowls and smoothies in a leafy garden.

do.name: Pai Canyon at sunset
do.what: Narrow ridges and drop-offs; go 5 pm, wear grippy shoes.

do.name: Tha Pai Hot Springs
do.what: Steamy natural pools in the forest; foreigners pay national park fee.

do.name: Boon Ko Ku So bamboo bridge
do.what: Long bamboo walkway over rice fields, best early with mist.

night.name: Walking Street
night.what: Night market: food carts, buskers, cheap souvenirs every evening.

night.name: Edible Jazz
night.what: Chill live acoustic and jazz in a garden, cushions on the floor.

night.name: Don’t Cry Bar
night.what: Party: riverside late-night bar where everyone ends up.

know: Only ride a scooter if you already can; the 762-curve road and gravel sends many tourists to Pai hospital.
Morning minivans from Chiang Mai cost about 200 to 250 baht; sit up front and skip a big breakfast.
December and January nights drop near 10 C; bring a fleece, bungalows rarely have heating.

cities.name: Chiang Rai
cities.getAround: Local buses run from the old bus terminal to the White Temple for about 20 to 30 baht. Grab works in town; a driver for a full temples day is roughly 1,200 to 1,800 baht per car.

timing.avoid: Mar to Apr: smoke and haze across the north. Jul to Sep: rainy season.
timing.note: Flower festival season runs Dec to Jan; the night bazaar is busiest at weekends.

vibe.line: Small, easygoing city with wild modern temples and tea hills next door.

eat.name: Saturday Walking Street, Thanalai Road
eat.what: Street food mile: sai oua, khanom krok, northern dips.

eat.name: Night Bazaar food court
eat.what: Hotpot, grilled fish and cheap beer by the live stage.

eat.name: Larb Lung Eed
eat.what: Northern-style larb with herbs and crispy pork skin; a local favourite.

do.name: Blue Temple (Wat Rong Suea Ten)
do.what: Electric-blue interior and white Buddha; free, less crowded than White Temple.

do.name: Baan Dam (Black House)
do.what: Dark, strange art compound of wooden halls and bones.

do.name: Singha Park
do.what: Cycle tea fields and lakes; flat, green, great for a slow afternoon.

night.name: Clock Tower light show
night.what: Golden tower lights up with music at 7, 8 and 9 pm; free.

night.name: Night Bazaar live stage
night.what: Chill: folk singers, cheap beer, families sharing hotpot.

know: Hit the White Temple at opening, then the Blue Temple; Grab between them is cheap and quick.
Green Bus from Chiang Mai is about 180 to 300 baht, depending on class, and very comfortable.
The Golden Triangle is underwhelming on rushed tours; spend that day at Doi Mae Salong tea village instead.

cities.name: Khao Sok
cities.getAround: Khlong Sok village is walkable to the park gate. Cheow Lan Lake is about an hour away: join a tour (day trip around 1,500 to 2,500 baht) or hire a longtail at the dam for a few thousand baht per boat.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: rainy, leeches on trails and some trails close. Oct to Nov is the wettest.
timing.note: Floating raft houses on the lake book out on Thai holidays; one to two nights is the sweet spot.

vibe.line: Ancient rainforest, misty limestone and floating lake huts with zero nightlife.

eat.name: Main road roti and fruit stalls
eat.what: Banana roti and shakes after a jungle walk.

eat.name: Phanom town market
eat.what: Real local market 20 minutes away: curries in bags, cheap fruit.

eat.name: Pawn’s Restaurant
eat.what: Friendly family kitchen; massaman and green curry done right.

do.name: Guided night jungle walk
do.what: Spot spiders, frogs, sleeping birds and maybe a tarantula.

do.name: Sok River tubing or canoe
do.what: Float under limestone cliffs, watch for monkeys.

do.name: Waterfall trail in the park
do.what: Easy self-guided walk to falls and swimming holes.

night.name: Stargazing from a lake raft house
night.what: Quiet: no lights, jungle sounds, millions of stars.

night.name: Riverside bungalow bars
night.what: Chill: a cold Chang by the river and early bed.

know: Book the Cheow Lan lake overnight in the village; Phuket and Krabi agents charge far more for the same raft.
After rain the trails are leech city; leech socks in the village cost about 100 to 150 baht.
There are a few ATMs on the main road, but they can run dry; arrive with enough cash.

cities.name: Krabi (Ao Nang and Railay)
cities.getAround: Longtails from Ao Nang to Railay cost about 100 to 150 baht one way and leave when full. Songthaews link Ao Nang and Krabi Town for about 60 to 80 baht; scooters rent for 200 to 300 baht a day.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: southwest monsoon, rough seas, fewer boats and some island trips cancelled.
timing.note: Christmas to mid January is the priciest stretch; book Railay rooms early.

vibe.line: Jaw-dropping limestone cliffs, longtail boats, climbers by day and fire shows by night.

eat.name: Krabi Town Night Market (Chao Fah)
eat.what: Weekend market: grilled squid, pad thai, half Ao Nang prices.

eat.name: Ao Nang Landmark Night Market
eat.what: Easy food court with seafood, curries and live music.

eat.name: Krua Thara
eat.what: Locals’ seafood spot: pick your fish, steamed with lime and chilli.

do.name: Rock climbing in Railay
do.what: Half day with a guide, no experience needed; world-class cliffs.

do.name: Kayak Ao Thalane
do.what: Paddle through mangroves and limestone canyons, quiet and green.

do.name: Hong Islands by longtail
do.what: Lagoon, white sand, snorkelling; go early to beat the speedboats.

night.name: Last Bar, Railay East
night.what: Party: fire show, buckets and Thai DJ under the cliffs.

night.name: Ao Nang Centre Point bars
night.what: Party: reggae and cocktail bars, loud till late.

night.name: Railay West sunset
night.what: Chill sunset spot: sand, cliffs and a beer from the stall.

know: Longtails from Ao Nang to Railay cost about 100 to 150 baht per person and leave when full.
Eat in Krabi Town on Friday to Sunday nights; same dishes as Ao Nang at roughly half price.
In rainy months, Railay boats can switch to Ao Nam Mao pier; ask at the beach ticket booth.

cities.name: Koh Phi Phi
cities.getAround: No roads: you walk. Longtails to beaches and viewpoints cost about 100 to 300 baht per person; a half-day longtail charter is roughly 1,500 to 3,000 baht per boat.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: rough seas, and Maya Bay closes every year for about two months (Aug to Sep).
timing.note: The island is loud at night near Tonsai and Loh Dalum; pick Long Beach or the north for quiet.

vibe.line: Turquoise bays by day, buckets and fire dancers on the sand by night.

eat.name: Roti carts in Tonsai Village
eat.what: Banana-Nutella roti at midnight, the island’s unofficial dessert.

eat.name: Tonsai local food market
eat.what: Cheap curries and fried rice near the pier, packed with workers.

eat.name: Papaya Restaurant
eat.what: Spicy, honest Thai food; the green curry and som tam are favourites.

do.name: Dawn longtail to Maya Bay and Pileh
do.what: Beat the speedboats; Maya Bay has a separate national park fee.

do.name: Bamboo Island trip
do.what: White sand and clear shallow water for snorkelling.

do.name: Kayak to Monkey Beach
do.what: Paddle round the headland, snorkel; keep food hidden from monkeys.

night.name: Loh Dalum beach bars
night.what: Party: fire shows, buckets, beach dance floor till late.

night.name: Reggae Bar
night.what: Party: drunk-tourist Muay Thai bouts and cheap drinks.

know: Buckets cost 250 to 450 baht on the beach; a 7-Eleven beer beforehand saves plenty.
Want sleep? Stay at the east end or Long Beach; Loh Dalum parties run until about 2 am.
Hire a private longtail at sunrise; split among friends it often costs less than a crowded speedboat tour.

cities.name: Phuket
cities.getAround: Smart Bus and pink songthaews run between Phuket Town and the main beaches for about 50 to 100 baht. Grab is often 300 to 600 baht to a beach; scooters rent for 200 to 350 baht a day.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: monsoon seas, red flags on west beaches and strong rip currents.
timing.note: The Vegetarian Festival (around Sep to Oct) fills Phuket Town with processions and meat-free street food.

vibe.line: Big island with colourful Sino-Portuguese old town, wild Patong nights and sunset capes.

eat.name: Lock Tien food court, Old Town
eat.what: Old-school stalls: Hokkien noodles, popiah, oyster omelette.

eat.name: Chillva Market
eat.what: Hip night market: grilled seafood, craft beer, container shops.

eat.name: One Chun
eat.what: Phuket-style crab curry and moo hong in a vintage shophouse.

do.name: Promthep Cape sunset
do.what: Phuket’s classic sunset, free; arrive early for a spot.

do.name: Big Buddha
do.what: Huge marble Buddha with island-wide views; cover knees and shoulders.

do.name: Phang Nga Bay day trip
do.what: Sea caves and limestone towers by boat and canoe.

night.name: Bangla Road, Patong
night.what: Full party: clubs, neon and touts; drinks cost bar prices.

night.name: Lard Yai Sunday Walking Street
night.what: Night market along Thalang Road, food and local crafts.

night.name: Timber Hut
night.what: Live music: Thai cover bands and a local crowd in Old Town.

know: Walk away from beach taxi stands and book Grab or Bolt; fares are often far lower.
The orange Smart Bus runs airport to Patong and Rawai for about 100 baht, versus 600 to 800 by taxi.
Stay in Old Town or Kata, not Patong, unless partying; food and rooms cost noticeably less.

cities.name: Koh Lanta
cities.getAround: Sidecar tuk-tuks cost about 100 to 400 baht depending on distance. Most visitors rent a scooter (200 to 300 baht a day) to roam the long west coast.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: many resorts and restaurants close, ferries are reduced and seas are rough.
timing.note: Lanta Lanta Festival in the Old Town in March celebrates the island's mix of cultures.

vibe.line: Long quiet beaches, hammocks and sunsets; the island where people slow right down.

eat.name: Saladan roti and som tam stalls
eat.what: Cheap snacks by the pier: roti, papaya salad, grilled chicken.

eat.name: Saladan market
eat.what: Local fruit, curries and fried snacks, cheaper than beach restaurants.

eat.name: Old Town stilt restaurants
eat.what: Seafood over the water on the quiet east coast.

do.name: Koh Rok snorkel trip
do.what: Best water around Lanta: reef fish and powder sand.

do.name: Scooter loop to Old Town
do.what: Ride the coast road to the Chinese-Muslim fishing village.

do.name: Lanta Animal Welfare
do.what: Visit or walk shelter dogs; free, donations welcome.

night.name: Long Beach sunset bars
night.what: Chill: bean bags on sand, fire twirlers, cheap cocktails.

night.name: Klong Nin beach bars
night.what: Chill: quiet reggae bars and sunset over the water.

know: May to October, many places close and boats shrink; prices fall but check your resort stays open.
Rent a scooter from your bungalow for about 250 baht a day; check brakes before the hilly south.
Lanta’s ATMs cluster in Saladan and Long Beach; withdraw there before heading south.

cities.name: Koh Samui
cities.getAround: Shared songthaews run round the ring road for about 50 to 150 baht. Taxis and Grab are pricey (300 to 700 baht across the island); scooters rent for 200 to 350 baht a day.

timing.avoid: Oct to Dec: the Gulf monsoon brings the heaviest rain and choppy ferry crossings.
timing.note: Fisherman's Village Walking Street runs Friday evenings; Full Moon parties on Koh Phangan fill Samui ferries.

vibe.line: Palm-lined beaches, beach clubs and villas; easy, polished island comfort.

eat.name: Lamai food court and night market
eat.what: Pad thai, BBQ skewers and shakes, island-cheap.

eat.name: Hua Thanon market
eat.what: Muslim fishing-village market: curries, roti, fresh fish.

eat.name: Krua Bophut
eat.what: Seafront Thai in Fisherman’s Village; book a sunset table.

do.name: Koh Tan and Koh Madsum by longtail
do.what: Quiet snorkelling islands off the south coast.

do.name: Na Muang Waterfall
do.what: Swim under falls in the jungle; free lower tier.

do.name: Secret Buddha Garden
do.what: Hilltop sculpture garden; 4x4 or confident scooter only.

night.name: Ark Bar Beach Club, Chaweng
night.what: Party: DJs on the sand, fire show, from afternoon till late.

night.name: Fisherman’s Village Walking Street
night.what: Friday night market: food, crafts, live music.

night.name: Coco Tam’s, Bophut
night.what: Chill: bean bags, fire show and cocktails on the beach.

know: Samui taxis rarely use meters; Grab or Bolt is usually much cheaper. Book from your lobby.
Songthaews run fixed routes on the ring road, roughly 50 to 100 baht by day, more after dark.
October to December is Samui’s rainy season, opposite the Andaman coast; November is often the wettest.

cities.name: Koh Tao
cities.getAround: Shared taxi pickups cost about 100 to 300 baht per person depending on the bay. Scooters rent for 200 to 300 baht a day, but the dirt roads are steep, so walk or take taxis if unsure.

timing.avoid: Oct to Dec: monsoon swell, ferry cancellations and poor visibility for diving.
timing.note: Whale shark sightings peak around Mar to May and Sep; diving is good most of the year outside the monsoon.

vibe.line: Tiny dive island: clear bays, scooter tracks and Sairee’s barefoot bar scene.

eat.name: Sairee pad thai and roti carts
eat.what: Late cheap eats after diving or a night out.

eat.name: Mae Haad night food stalls
eat.what: Local dinners by the pier: noodles, grilled meat, fruit.

eat.name: Su Chili
eat.what: Spicy, generous Thai plates; a diver favourite in Sairee.

do.name: Open Water dive course
do.what: One of the world’s cheapest; 3 to 4 days, often with a room deal.

do.name: Snorkel Shark Bay
do.what: Swim off the beach; black-tip reef sharks in the mornings.

do.name: Round-island longtail snorkel trip
do.what: Hits several bays plus Koh Nang Yuan in one day.

night.name: Lotus Bar, Sairee
night.what: Party: fire shows and beach dancing, especially Wednesdays and weekends.

night.name: Fizz Beach Lounge
night.what: Chill: bean bags, sunset cocktails, soft music.

night.name: Sairee Beach sunset
night.what: Free sunset spot; grab a 7-Eleven beer and sit on the sand.

know: Dive schools give cheap or free rooms during courses; ask before booking a room yourself.
Photograph your rental scooter before riding; some shops charge for old scratches on return.
Seas get rough November to December; take seasickness pills before the catamaran from Samui or Chumphon.

cities.name: Koh Phangan
cities.getAround: Shared songthaews and taxi pickups; there is no Grab. Scooters are about 200 to 300 baht a day, but the hills are steep: only ride if experienced. On party nights a shared taxi from Thong Sala to Haad Rin is about 200 to 400 baht per person.

timing.avoid: Oct to Dec: the Gulf's heaviest rain
timing.note: Full moon week: room prices can double and many places ask for 3 to 5 night minimum stays.

vibe.line: Full moon madness in Haad Rin, yoga and quiet coves everywhere else.

eat.name: Thong Sala Night Market
eat.what: Grilled seafood, pad thai, mango sticky rice and fruit shakes every evening.

eat.name: Haad Rin street food lanes
eat.what: Noodles and toasties before the party; cheap, fast, open late.

eat.name: Srithanu cafés
eat.what: The island's yoga village: vegan bowls, smoothies and good coffee.

do.name: Bottle Beach (Haad Khuad)
do.what: A quiet bay in the north, best reached by longtail boat.

do.name: Than Sadet waterfall and beach
do.what: Royal waterfall stream down to a wild east-coast cove.

do.name: Koh Ma sandbar
do.what: Walk across a sandbar to a tiny island; good snorkelling.

night.name: Full Moon Party, Haad Rin Sunrise Beach
night.what: Party: tens of thousands, neon paint, buckets, fire shows till sunrise.

night.name: Half Moon and Jungle parties
night.what: Rave: jungle stages near Ban Tai a week before and after the full moon.

night.name: West coast sunset bars
night.what: Chill: beanbags, DJs and sunset over the sea.

know: Book full moon rooms weeks ahead; many places sell 3 to 5 night packages, and prices often double.
Buckets are strong and cheap spirits: buy sealed drinks at 7-Eleven, wear shoes (broken glass), keep phone and cash in a zip bag.
Stay the night after the party: late boats back to Samui and Koh Tao are packed and the sea can be rough.

cities.name: Koh Chang
cities.getAround: Shared songthaews run the west coast road for about 50 to 100 baht a hop, more after dark. Scooters rent for 200 to 300 baht a day, but the hills are steep; a songthaew charter for the day is about 1,000 to 1,500 baht.

timing.avoid: Jun to Sep: monsoon rain, rough seas and fewer boats to Koh Kood and Koh Mak.
timing.note: New Year and Thai long weekends bring long queues for the car ferry; cross early.

vibe.line: Jungle hills, easy beaches and a stilted fishing pier: an island with room for everyone.

eat.name: Bang Bao pier seafood
eat.what: Restaurants on stilts over the water: crab, squid, whole fish by weight.

eat.name: Salak Phet stilt restaurants
eat.what: Crab and seafood over the mangroves, cheaper and calmer than the west coast.

eat.name: White Sand Beach roadside stalls
eat.what: Pad kra pao, noodles and fruit along the main road at night.

do.name: Klong Plu Waterfall
do.what: Swim under the falls; park fee applies.

do.name: Southern islands snorkel boat
do.what: Day boat from Bang Bao to Koh Rang and nearby reefs, lunch included.

do.name: Salak Kok mangrove kayak
do.what: Community-run kayaks through quiet mangrove channels.

night.name: Lonely Beach bars
night.what: Party: backpacker bars with buckets and DJs till late.

night.name: White Sand Beach fire shows
night.what: Chill: beanbags, cocktails and fire dancers on the sand.

know: The car ferry is the cheapest crossing; walk-on passengers pay about 80 to 100 baht.
Koh Chang's hill roads cause many scooter crashes; if in doubt, take songthaews.
Island-hopping boats to Koh Mak and Koh Kood mostly run November to May; check before low season trips.

cities.name: Koh Kood
cities.getAround: There is no public transport. Resorts pick you up at the pier; scooters rent for about 250 to 350 baht a day on hilly roads, and pickup truck taxis charge about 100 to 300 baht a ride.

timing.avoid: Jun to Sep: many resorts and speedboats close or cut back, seas are rough.
timing.note: December and January weekends fill fast with Thai visitors; book rooms with transfers early.

vibe.line: Glassy water, empty bays and a waterfall swim: an island for switching off.

eat.name: Ao Salad crab houses
eat.what: Steamed blue crab and squid over the water in the fishing village.

eat.name: Klong Chao village kitchens
eat.what: Curries, fried rice and noodle soup at local prices near the river.

eat.name: Ao Yai stilt village
eat.what: Simple seafood and coffee shops in an old village on stilts.

do.name: Klong Chao Waterfall
do.what: Swim in the big pool below the falls; go before noon.

do.name: Kayak Klong Chao river
do.what: Paddle up a mangrove river from the beach to the village.

do.name: Snorkel trip to Koh Rang
do.what: Boat trips to clearer reefs in the marine park.

night.name: Resort beach bars
night.what: Chill: sunset drinks on the west coast; nights are quiet and starry.

night.name: Klong Chao bridge at dusk
night.what: Chill: watch the river turn pink and the fishing boats come home.

know: ATMs are few; bring enough cash from Trat or Koh Chang.
Book a room that includes pier transfers, or you may wait a long time for a ride.
Speedboats from Koh Chang run mainly in high season; in low season you go via Laem Sok pier on the mainland.

cities.name: Koh Mak
cities.getAround: The island is flat and small. Bicycles rent for about 50 to 100 baht a day and scooters for 250 to 300; resorts pick up from the pier.

timing.avoid: Jun to Sep: boats are fewer and many places close.
timing.note: A good break between Koh Chang and Koh Kood; one or two nights is enough for most.

vibe.line: Bicycles, sandbars and coconut groves: a sleepy island with no rush at all.

eat.name: Ao Nid pier eateries
eat.what: Noodles, rice dishes and fresh fish near the main pier.

eat.name: Ao Kao beach restaurants
eat.what: Thai and seafood with your feet in the sand at sunset.

eat.name: Village cafes
eat.what: Iced coffee and snacks at small cafes along the main road.

do.name: Kayak to Koh Kham
do.what: Paddle to the islet for clear water; landing fee applies.

do.name: Bike the plantations
do.what: Loop the island on shady rubber and coconut lanes.

do.name: Snorkel trip to Koh Rang
do.what: Day boat to the marine park reefs.

night.name: Ao Kao beach bars
night.what: Chill: low-key reggae bars and bonfires.

night.name: Night sky
night.what: Chill: so little light you can see the stars from the jetty.

know: Bring cash; ATMs are limited and some resorts charge for card payments.
There are no jet skis or big parties; that is the point.
Boats to Koh Chang and Koh Kood are seasonal, mainly November to May.

cities.name: Koh Samet
cities.getAround: Shared green songthaews run from Na Dan pier to the beaches for about 30 to 100 baht per person. Scooters and ATVs rent for 300 to 500 baht a day; the roads are dusty dirt tracks.

timing.avoid: Weekends and Thai long weekends, when Bangkok crowds fill rooms and prices jump.
timing.note: Samet gets less rain than most of Thailand, so it is a fair bet even in the wet season.

vibe.line: Soft sand close to Bangkok: beach dinners, fire shows and quiet coves to the south.

eat.name: Na Dan pier stalls
eat.what: Som tam, grilled chicken and noodles before or after the ferry.

eat.name: Hat Sai Kaew seafood barbecue
eat.what: Choose from the ice and eat at candlelit tables on the beach.

eat.name: Ao Wong Duean beach restaurants
eat.what: Thai dishes and seafood on a calm, sheltered bay.

do.name: Coastal path walk
do.what: Walk south bay to bay from Hat Sai Kaew; free and lovely.

do.name: Snorkel boat trip
do.what: Half or full day to Koh Kudi and nearby islets.

do.name: Sunset at Ao Prao
do.what: Cross the island for the only west-facing beach.

night.name: Ao Phai beach bars
night.what: Party: buckets, music and late nights on the sand.

night.name: Hat Sai Kaew fire shows
night.what: Chill: fire dancers after dinner on the main beach.

know: Every visitor pays the park fee at the entry point; keep your ticket.
Ferries leave Ban Phe pier hourly or when full; speedboats cost more but drop you at your beach.
Bring cash for the beaches south of Ao Wong Duean; card machines are rare.

cities.name: Pattaya
cities.getAround: Baht buses (shared songthaews) loop Beach Road and Second Road for about 10 to 20 baht; just hop on and press the buzzer. Grab and Bolt cost about 80 to 200 baht across town, scooters 200 to 300 baht a day.

timing.avoid: Sep to Oct: heavy showers and grey seas. Holiday weekends: traffic from Bangkok crawls.
timing.note: Fireworks festival in late November, music festival weekends in March, and Wan Lai water fights in mid April.

vibe.line: Loud, neon and unapologetic: go-go bars on one street, family beaches and a wooden temple on the next.

eat.name: Lan Pho Naklua fish market
eat.what: Buy seafood fresh and have it grilled next door.

eat.name: Thepprasit Night Market
eat.what: Fri to Sun: grilled skewers, seafood, desserts and cheap shopping.

eat.name: Jomtien Night Market
eat.what: Easygoing food stalls by the beach, good for families.

do.name: Sanctuary of Truth
do.what: Hand-carved wooden temple by the sea; dress modestly.

do.name: Koh Larn by public ferry
do.what: From Bali Hai pier to Tawaen or Samae beach.

do.name: Khao Chi Chan
do.what: A giant Buddha outline in gold on a cliff face, south of town.

night.name: Walking Street
night.what: Party: neon strip of clubs, live bands and go-go bars; loud, adult and not for everyone.

night.name: Cabaret show
night.what: Show: glittering ladyboy cabaret, big costumes, family friendly.

night.name: Thepprasit Night Market
night.what: Night market: Fri to Sun, food and bargains till late.

know: Do not climb into an empty baht bus without asking; it may be treated as a private charter at a much higher price.
Jet ski damage scams are common: photograph the machine before you ride, or skip it.
On Walking Street, check drink prices first and avoid bars with touts pulling you in.

cities.name: Hua Hin
cities.getAround: Green shared songthaews run along Phetkasem Road for about 15 to 20 baht. Grab and Bolt cost about 80 to 200 baht in town; scooters rent for 200 to 300 baht a day.

timing.avoid: Oct to Nov: the heaviest rain on this coast.
timing.note: Cicada and Tamarind markets open Friday to Sunday evenings; Bangkok families fill hotels on long weekends.

vibe.line: Royal seaside town: long beach, great night markets and an unhurried, grown-up pace.

eat.name: Hua Hin Night Market
eat.what: Seafood grills, roti and mango sticky rice on Dechanuchit Road.

eat.name: Chatchai Market
eat.what: Morning market for khanom krok, patongko and soy milk.

eat.name: Khao Takiab seafood
eat.what: Simple seafood restaurants by the fishing boats.

do.name: Phraya Nakhon Cave
do.what: Climb to the royal pavilion in a sunlit cave; about an hour's drive south.

do.name: Hua Hin Railway Station
do.what: Photo stop at the old wooden station and royal pavilion.

do.name: Maruekhathaiyawan Palace
do.what: Teak summer palace on stilts, breezy and photogenic.

night.name: Cicada Market
night.what: Night market: Fri to Sun art, crafts, live music and a food court.

night.name: Tamarind Market
night.what: Night market: food stalls and live bands next to Cicada.

night.name: Soi Bintabaht
night.what: Party: small bar lane in the old town, a little seedy but lively.

know: Horse rides on the beach are pushed hard; agree price and time before you get on.
The Khao Takiab monkeys snatch food and bags, so keep both hidden.
Third class trains from Bangkok cost very little but take longer; reserved seats sell out on weekends.

cities.name: Khao Yai
cities.getAround: You need wheels. Rent a car (about 1,000 to 1,500 baht a day) or join a guided park tour (about 1,200 to 1,800 baht with lunch). A songthaew runs from Pak Chong to near the park gate for about 40 baht.

timing.avoid: Thai long weekends: traffic jams on the park road. Jul to Oct: leeches on trails, though waterfalls are full.
timing.note: Nights in December and January can drop near 12 C; pack a jacket.

vibe.line: Elephants by day, wineries and cosy cafes by evening: Bangkok's green weekend escape.

eat.name: Pak Chong Night Market
eat.what: Roast duck noodles, grilled pork and Thai desserts.

eat.name: Thanarat Road corn and milk stalls
eat.what: Sweet grilled corn and cold local milk.

eat.name: PB Valley winery
eat.what: Thai wine tastings and lunch with vineyard views.

do.name: Guided wildlife day tour
do.what: Gibbons, hornbills and elephants with a spotting scope.

do.name: Haew Suwat Waterfall
do.what: Classic falls inside the park; park ticket needed.

do.name: Bat cave at dusk
do.what: Watch millions of bats leave Khao Luk Chang at sunset.

night.name: Pak Chong Night Market
night.what: Night market: food and fresh fruit in the town centre.

night.name: Cafe and campfire evenings
night.what: Chill: glamping sites and cafes along Thanarat Road with fire pits.

know: Foreigners buy park tickets through the QueQ app or at the gate; carry your passport.
Never feed or approach elephants on the road; keep the engine running and back off slowly.
Most visitors come by car; public transport only reaches Pak Chong town, about 30 km from the park.

cities.name: Amphawa
cities.getAround: Walk along the canal paths. Longtail boats and firefly rides cost about 60 to 100 baht per person shared; songthaews to Maeklong town are about 10 to 20 baht.

timing.best: Nov to Feb, Fri to Sun
timing.avoid: Mon to Thu: most of the market is closed.
timing.note: The market runs about noon to 9 pm on Friday to Sunday; Maeklong Railway Market sees trains several times a day.

vibe.line: Wooden houses, canal boats and grilled prawns: Bangkok's favourite weekend food trip.

eat.name: Amphawa canal boat kitchens
eat.what: Grilled prawns, squid and noodles cooked on boats.

eat.name: Canal-side snack stalls
eat.what: Coconut ice cream, khanom and iced drinks along the banks.

eat.name: Maeklong Railway Market stalls
eat.what: Fresh fruit and snacks between train passes.

do.name: Firefly boat ride
do.what: Evening longtail through dark canals.

do.name: Maeklong Railway Market
do.what: Watch stalls fold away for the train; check times.

do.name: Wat Bang Kung
do.what: Chapel wrapped in tree roots, 15 minutes away.

night.name: Amphawa canal at dusk
night.what: Night market: lanterns, boat kitchens and crowds till about 9 pm.

night.name: Homestay riverside decks
night.what: Chill: a cold drink on the water once the crowds leave.

know: Amphawa is a Friday to Sunday market; on weekdays it is a sleepy village.
Damnoen Saduak is a morning tour-bus market; arrive by 7 am and agree boat prices first.
Canal homestays can be noisy until the market closes; ask for a room away from the main bridge.

cities.name: Lopburi
cities.getAround: The old town is walkable from the station. Samlors and tuk-tuks charge about 40 to 80 baht a hop; songthaews to the new town are 10 to 20 baht.

timing.avoid: Mar to May: very hot, often above 37 C.
timing.note: The Monkey Buffet is held near the end of November; sunflower fields bloom November to January.

vibe.line: Khmer towers, a royal palace and a town that belongs to the monkeys.

eat.name: Station food stalls
eat.what: Noodles, rice dishes and iced coffee by the railway.

eat.name: Old town fresh market
eat.what: Morning patongko, soy milk and curries over rice.

eat.name: Na Phra Kan Road noodle shops
eat.what: Boat noodles and khao man gai near the shrine.

do.name: Phra Prang Sam Yot
do.what: Khmer towers full of monkeys; remove anything loose.

do.name: Phra Narai Ratchaniwet
do.what: Palace grounds and museum; closed Mon and Tue.

do.name: Sunflower fields
do.what: Drive or join a tour east of town, November to January.

night.name: Old town evening stalls
night.what: Night market: grilled meats and desserts near the railway.

night.name: Prang Sam Yot after dark
night.what: Chill: the lit towers and a quiet walk once the monkeys sleep.

know: Monkeys grab glasses, hats, phones and anything in plastic bags; keep everything in a zipped bag.
Most visitors stop for half a day between Ayutthaya and the north; the station has left luggage.
Trains are cheap and frequent from Bangkok and Ayutthaya; check return times before you explore.

cities.name: Koh Yao Noi
cities.getAround: Rent a scooter for about 250 to 300 baht a day or a bicycle for 100 to 150; tuk-tuk taxis charge about 100 to 200 baht a ride. Longtails to nearby islands cost about 1,500 to 3,000 baht per boat for a half day.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: monsoon rain and choppier boat rides, though the bay is sheltered.
timing.note: During Ramadan many village food shops open only after sunset.

vibe.line: Rice fields, buffaloes and limestone towers at sunrise: the slow way to see Phang Nga Bay.

eat.name: Tha Khao village kitchens
eat.what: Roti, chicken curry and southern rice dishes.

eat.name: Seafood by Manoh pier
eat.what: Crab, fish and squid from local boats.

eat.name: Island cafes on the ring road
eat.what: Coffee, smoothies and Thai plates with paddy views.

do.name: Longtail to Koh Hong lagoon
do.what: Early boat to the hidden lagoon before the tour boats; fee applies.

do.name: Phang Nga Bay canoe tour
do.what: Sea canoe into the hongs with a guide.

do.name: Island loop by scooter
do.what: Paddy fields, rubber farms and fishing villages.

night.name: Resort beach bars
night.what: Chill: sunset drinks facing the karsts.

night.name: Village night stalls
night.what: Night market: grilled chicken, roti and sweets after dark.

know: It is a Muslim island: cover shoulders and knees in villages and ask before photographing people.
Bring cash; there are only a few ATMs.
Boats from Phuket's Bang Rong pier and from Krabi's Tha Len pier make it easy to reach.

cities.name: Khao Lak (Similan base)
cities.getAround: Most tours include hotel pickup. Taxis and songthaews charge about 200 to 500 baht a trip along the coast; scooters rent for about 250 baht a day.

timing.best: Mid Oct to mid May (park open)
timing.avoid: Mid May to mid Oct: the park is closed.
timing.note: Clearest water and manta season is about February to April; book boats early in December and January.

vibe.line: Quiet beach town on the mainland, launch pad for the Andaman's best diving.

eat.name: Bang Niang Market
eat.what: Evening market with curries, grilled fish and fruit shakes on set days.

eat.name: Khao Lak roadside seafood
eat.what: Simple restaurants grilling the day's catch.

eat.name: Takua Pa Old Town
eat.what: Sino-Portuguese shophouses with noodles and southern sweets.

do.name: Similan day trip
do.what: Speedboat with 3 to 4 snorkel stops, lunch and pickup; park fee often extra.

do.name: Dive day trip
do.what: Two or three dives in the Similans from Khao Lak.

do.name: Police Boat 813 memorial
do.what: A boat swept inland by the 2004 tsunami, now a quiet memorial.

night.name: Khao Lak beach bars
night.what: Chill: sunset drinks and seafood dinners on Nang Thong beach.

night.name: Bang Niang Market
night.what: Night market: food and souvenirs a few evenings a week.

know: The park limits daily visitors, so book day trips a few days ahead in peak season.
Overnight stays on the islands may not be allowed; plan day trips or a liveaboard.
Harmful sunscreen is banned in the park; bring a coral-safe one or a rash guard.

cities.name: Koh Lipe
cities.getAround: Everything is walkable on sandy paths. Motorbike taxis charge about 50 to 100 baht; longtails to snorkel spots run about 500 to 800 baht per person shared, or 1,500 to 2,500 baht per boat.

timing.avoid: Mid May to mid Oct: few boats, rough seas and many places closed.
timing.note: Christmas, New Year and Chinese New Year fill the island; book boats and rooms early.

vibe.line: Tiny, walkable and ringed by clear water: the far south's island escape.

eat.name: Walking Street stalls
eat.what: Roti, grilled skewers, curries and shakes.

eat.name: Pattaya Beach seafood
eat.what: Barbecue from the ice, tables on the sand.

eat.name: Sea gypsy village kitchens
eat.what: Simple Thai dishes in the Urak Lawoi village near Sunrise Beach.

do.name: Longtail snorkel trip
do.what: Koh Hin Ngam, Koh Rawi and nearby reefs in a day.

do.name: Chado Cliff, Koh Adang
do.what: Steep hike to a view over Lipe.

do.name: Sunset Beach
do.what: Quiet west-facing cove for golden hour.

night.name: Walking Street
night.what: Night market: food, shops and buskers every evening.

night.name: Sunrise Beach bars
night.what: Chill: fire shows and cushions on the sand.

night.name: Pattaya Beach reggae bars
night.what: Party: buckets and music till late.

know: Bring enough cash; ATMs exist but charge fees and can run out in peak weeks.
There is no big pier on Lipe: speedboats may transfer you to a longtail or floating pontoon for a small extra fee.
Boats link Lipe with Langkawi in Malaysia, with immigration on the island.

cities.name: Mae Hong Son
cities.getAround: The town is walkable. Scooters rent for about 200 to 250 baht a day; a songthaew or car with driver to Pang Ung and Ban Rak Thai costs about 1,200 to 1,800 baht for the trip.

timing.avoid: Mar to Apr: smoky haze from field burning. Jul to Sep: slippery mountain roads.
timing.note: Wild sunflowers bloom on Doi Mae U Kho from mid November to early December; Poy Sang Long ordinations around late March or early April.

vibe.line: Misty valleys, Shan temples on a lake and a long, curvy road to get here.

eat.name: Chong Kham lake night market
eat.what: Shan snacks, grilled meats and noodles by the lit temples.

eat.name: Morning market
eat.what: Khao kan jin, tua nao and Shan curries at dawn.

eat.name: Ban Rak Thai tea houses
eat.what: Yunnan tea tastings and dumplings by the lake.

do.name: Doi Kong Mu sunrise
do.what: Hilltop temple over a valley of mist.

do.name: Pang Ung at dawn
do.what: Pine forest lake and bamboo rafts in fog.

do.name: Su Tong Pae Bridge
do.what: Walk the bamboo bridge over rice paddies.

night.name: Chong Kham walking street
night.what: Night market: lakeside stalls in the cool season.

night.name: Lakeside cafes
night.what: Chill: hot drinks facing the lit temple reflections.

know: The Mae Hong Son loop has thousands of curves; take motion sickness pills for minivans.
Mornings can be near 10 C from December to January; bring a warm layer.
Long-neck Karen villages charge entry and are debated; if you go, choose a community-run visit and buy crafts directly.

cities.name: Chiang Dao
cities.getAround: Most guesthouses are along the cave road, 5 km from the market town. Scooters rent for 200 to 300 baht a day; songthaews between town and the cave are about 30 to 50 baht, and guesthouses arrange drivers for about 1,000 to 1,500 baht a day.

timing.avoid: Mar to Apr: smoky haze from field burning hides the mountain.
timing.note: Cool-season weekends fill quickly with Thai visitors; book ahead.

vibe.line: Garden bungalows under a limestone giant, birdsong and slow mornings.

eat.name: Chiang Dao Nest restaurant
eat.what: Long-running garden restaurant with Thai and European plates under the cliffs.

eat.name: Tuesday morning market
eat.what: Hill tribe market with snacks, khao soi and vegetables.

eat.name: Cave road noodle shops
eat.what: Simple kitchens for khao soi and fried rice near the cave.

do.name: Chiang Dao Cave
do.what: Lantern-lit cave temple deep in the mountain.

do.name: Wat Tham Pha Plong
do.what: Forest temple up about 500 steps with mountain views.

do.name: Birdwatching walk
do.what: Guided early walks in the forest below Doi Luang, a top birding area.

night.name: Guesthouse terraces
night.what: Chill: a cold beer with the mountain turning pink at dusk.

night.name: Small jazz and reggae bars on the cave road
night.what: Chill: a couple of tiny bars with live music some nights.

know: Bring cash; there are ATMs in town but few by the cave.
Nights are cold in December and January; pack a fleece.
The Doi Luang summit trek needs a licensed local guide and opens only in the cool season with daily limits.
cities.stayArea: Stay on the cave road at the foot of Doi Luang, where garden bungalows look straight at the mountain.

cities.name: Nan
cities.getAround: The old town is compact and flat: bicycles rent for about 50 to 100 baht a day and scooters for 200 to 300. For Doi Phu Kha and Bo Kluea, hire a car with driver for about 1,800 to 2,500 baht a day.

timing.avoid: Mar to Apr: haze from burning. Jun to Sep: rain closes some mountain trails.
timing.note: The boat races around October and November and New Year fill rooms.

vibe.line: A quiet valley town of murals, golden stupas and mountain roads.

eat.name: Walking street food by Wat Phumin
eat.what: Weekend evening stalls with Nan noodles and grilled snacks.

eat.name: Nan riverside night market
eat.what: Evening stalls along the river for grilled fish and larb.

eat.name: Old town cafes
eat.what: Wooden houses turned into cafes serving Nan coffee and cakes.

do.name: Wat Phumin
do.what: The famous murals of everyday Nan life.

do.name: Nan National Museum
do.what: A palace museum with a sacred black elephant tusk.

do.name: Doi Phu Kha and Bo Kluea day trip
do.what: Mountain views and the old salt wells.

night.name: Kad Khuang Mueang Nan walking street
night.what: Market: Friday to Sunday evenings beside Wat Phumin, with folk music.

night.name: Riverside bars
night.what: Chill: a few relaxed bars with live acoustic sets along the Nan River.

know: Nan is far from other hubs; the Bangkok flight saves a long bus day.
Mountain roads to Bo Kluea are steep and winding; avoid driving them at night.
Temples here are still very much in use; dress modestly and keep voices low.
cities.stayArea: Stay in the old town within cycling distance of Wat Phumin and the weekend walking street.

cities.name: Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat)
cities.getAround: A big, spread-out city: Grab and songthaews (about 10 to 15 baht a ride) work in town. Buses run to Phimai about hourly for about 50 to 70 baht, 1 h 15 min. For Phanom Rung, hire a car with driver for about 2,000 to 3,000 baht a day.

timing.avoid: Mar to May: very hot on exposed temple sites.
timing.note: Plan around the Phanom Rung sun alignments in March, April, September and October if you can.

vibe.line: The gateway to Isaan: Khmer temples, night markets and real local life.

eat.name: Wat Boon night market
eat.what: A big local night market for grilled meats, noodles and sweets.

eat.name: Phimai noodle shops
eat.what: Pad Mi Phimai near the temple in Phimai town.

eat.name: Isaan grill houses
eat.what: Som tam, gai yang and larb at simple open-air restaurants.

do.name: Thao Suranari Monument
do.what: The city's beloved heroine, surrounded by offerings and dancers.

do.name: Phimai Historical Park
do.what: Restored Khmer temple an hour from town.

do.name: Phanom Rung day trip
do.what: Volcano-top Khmer temple with Prasat Muang Tam.

night.name: Wat Boon night market
night.what: Market: crowded and cheap, best after 6 pm.

night.name: Isaan live music bars
night.what: Party: mor lam bands and local beer in lively bars near the moat.

know: Korat is the gateway to Khao Yai too; it is about 1 to 1.5 hours away by bus.
English is less common than in tourist towns; a translation app helps.
Buses to Bangkok leave often from Bus Terminal 2 (Bor Kor Sor 2).
cities.stayArea: Stay inside the old moat near the Thao Suranari Monument, close to the markets and the bus to Phimai.

cities.name: Udon Thani
cities.getAround: Songthaews and tuk-tuks cover town for about 20 to 100 baht; Grab works too. For the Red Lotus Sea, hire a car with driver for about 1,200 to 1,800 baht for the morning, or join a sunrise tour.

timing.avoid: Mar to May: very hot. Aug to Oct: heavy rain.
timing.note: The Red Lotus Sea blooms only from about December to February.

vibe.line: A friendly Isaan city of lotus lakes, Bronze Age relics and great markets.

eat.name: UD Town night market
eat.what: Food stalls and craft shops around a modern open-air hub.

eat.name: Thung Si Mueang night market
eat.what: Local evening market for Isaan food in the city park.

eat.name: Vietnamese restaurants
eat.what: Naem nuang pork rolls, a local speciality from the Vietnamese community.

do.name: Red Lotus Sea at sunrise
do.what: Boat ride through a lake of pink lotus.

do.name: Ban Chiang National Museum
do.what: World Heritage Bronze Age site.

do.name: Nong Prajak Park
do.what: A lake park for walks, bikes and evening aerobics.

night.name: UD Town
night.what: Chill: open-air bars and live music around the night market.

night.name: Prajak Road bars
night.what: Party: lively local bars and live bands.

know: The lotus flowers close by late morning; leave town by 5:30 am.
Udon has good air links, so it is the easiest gateway to Isaan and to Chiang Khan.
Nong Khai and the Friendship Bridge to Laos are about an hour north.
cities.stayArea: Stay near UD Town and the train station, central for markets, buses and the airport.

cities.name: Chiang Khan
cities.getAround: The whole town is walkable along Chai Khong Road. Bicycles rent for about 50 to 100 baht a day; songthaews do the sunrise run to Phu Thok for about 30 to 50 baht per person.

timing.avoid: Mar to May: hot and hazy, no sea of mist.
timing.note: Cool-season weekends are very busy; weekdays feel like a different town.

vibe.line: Wooden houses, Mekong sunsets and a walking street every evening.

eat.name: Walking street stalls
eat.what: Snacks, khao poon and grilled river fish each evening.

eat.name: Riverside restaurants
eat.what: Mekong fish and Isaan dishes with a view of Laos.

eat.name: Kaeng Khut Khu stalls
eat.what: Coconut sweets and grilled snacks by the rapids.

do.name: Phu Thok sunrise
do.what: Sea of mist at dawn in the cool season.

do.name: Morning alms
do.what: Monks walk Chai Khong Road around 6 am.

do.name: Cycle the Mekong
do.what: Ride the river road to Kaeng Khut Khu.

night.name: Chiang Khan Walking Street
night.what: Market: the whole riverfront road from about 5 to 10 pm.

night.name: Riverside cafe bars
night.what: Chill: acoustic music in wooden houses on the river.

know: Book riverside rooms ahead for weekends from November to January.
The nearest airport is Loei, about an hour away; Udon Thani has more flights.
The Phi Ta Khon ghost festival at Dan Sai is about two hours south, usually in June or early July.
cities.stayArea: Stay in a wooden guesthouse on Chai Khong Road, right on the walking street and the river.

cities.name: Trang Islands (Koh Ngai, Kradan, Mook)
cities.getAround: Longtails link the islands for about 300 to 800 baht per person a hop, or charter one for about 1,500 to 2,500 baht a day. Daily speedboats in season connect Koh Ngai, Kradan and Mook with Lanta and Lipe. On the mainland, minivans run from Trang town to Pak Meng pier in about 45 minutes.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: monsoon seas, fewer boats and many resorts closed.
timing.note: The underwater wedding near Koh Kradan around Valentine's Day books up rooms.

vibe.line: Small quiet islands with coral off the beach and a cave lagoon.

eat.what: Southern curries and roti in the Muslim village.

eat.name: Koh Ngai resort restaurants
eat.what: Beachfront seafood and Thai dishes.

eat.name: Trang town dim sum

night.name: Kradan Sunset Beach
night.what: Chill: a short jungle walk to a west-facing beach.

know: Bring cash: ATMs are scarce on the islands.
Check whether your resort closes for the low season before booking May to October.
Go to the Emerald Cave at low tide; at high tide the tunnel can be closed.
cities.stayArea: Base on Koh Mook for village life and cheaper rooms, Koh Kradan for the best beach, or Koh Ngai for calm, family-friendly resorts.

cities.name: Koh Phayam
cities.getAround: No cars: scooters rent for about 250 to 350 baht a day, and motorbike taxis from the pier to the beaches cost about 70 to 150 baht. Speedboats and slow boats run from Ranong pier.

timing.avoid: May to Oct: heavy Andaman rain, rough crossings and many closures.
timing.note: Ranong is one of Thailand's wettest provinces, so the dry season matters here.

vibe.line: No cars, no crowds: cashew trees, hammocks and long sunset beaches.

eat.name: Phayam village restaurants
eat.what: Thai food and fresh seafood near the pier.

eat.name: Ao Yai beach kitchens
eat.what: Bungalow restaurants with curries and grilled fish.

eat.name: Buffalo Bay cafes

do.name: Snorkel trip to nearby islands
do.what: Longtail day trips in calm weather.

do.name: Hornbill spotting
do.what: Great hornbills often fly over at dawn.

night.what: Chill: driftwood bars, fire shows and reggae.

night.name: Buffalo Bay sunset bars
night.what: Chill: swings and cocktails as the sun sets over Myanmar's islands.

know: Bring cash from Ranong; island ATMs are few and unreliable.
The last boats back to Ranong leave mid-afternoon.
Ranong is also the crossing to Kawthaung in Myanmar; check current rules before trying it.
cities.stayArea: Stay on Ao Yai for the longest beach and most bars, or Buffalo Bay for a quieter, prettier cove.

wishIKnew.title: Buy your beer at 7-Eleven
wishIKnew.tip: 7-Eleven: Leo 490 ml about 53 baht, Chang 53 to 55, Singha 56. Bars charge 80 to 150, rooftops 300 plus. A SangSom flask is roughly 150 to 250.

wishIKnew.title: Alcohol sells 11 am to midnight
wishIKnew.tip: Since late May 2026, shops and restaurants sell 11:00 to midnight; the old 2 to 5 pm ban is gone. No sales on Buddhist holy days.

wishIKnew.title: After-hours drinking can be fined
wishIKnew.tip: Since Nov 2025, customers caught drinking outside legal hours at unlicensed places risk fines up to 10,000 baht. Licensed clubs in nightlife zones can serve later.

wishIKnew.title: Withdraw big, withdraw rarely
wishIKnew.tip: Foreign cards pay about 220 to 350 baht per ATM withdrawal. Take 20,000 to 30,000 at once, decline the conversion, try AEON ATMs (about 150).

wishIKnew.title: Change money at SuperRich
wishIKnew.tip: Skip arrival-hall booths. SuperRich (orange) in Suvarnabhumi basement, by the Rail Link, or in town pays noticeably better. Clean, unmarked USD notes get the best rate.

wishIKnew.title: Rail Link beats the taxi
wishIKnew.tip: Airport Rail Link to Phaya Thai: 45 baht, about 26 minutes. A taxi runs roughly 300 to 500 with the 50 baht airport fee, tolls and traffic.

wishIKnew.title: Street food costs a third
wishIKnew.tip: Pad krapao or noodles cost 50 to 80 baht at stalls, 150 to 300 in tourist restaurants. Follow office workers at lunch for the best spots.

wishIKnew.title: 7-Eleven is your safety net
wishIKnew.tip: Ham and cheese toastie 30 to 45 baht, microwave meals 40 to 70, staff heat them free. Also cheap sunscreen, medicine, SIM top-ups.

wishIKnew.title: Grab first, tuk-tuk for fun
wishIKnew.tip: Grab or Bolt short city hops run about 60 to 150 baht; tuk-tuks quote 150 to 300. Ride one once for the photo, agree the price first.

wishIKnew.title: Shared songthaew, not charter
wishIKnew.tip: Chiang Mai red trucks cost about 30 to 40 baht shared in town. If the driver says charter or names 150 plus, it’s private. Wave the next.

wishIKnew.title: Grand Palace: dress and scam
wishIKnew.tip: “Palace closed today” is a scam leading to gem shops; walk to the gate yourself. Cover shoulders and knees; elephant pants cost 100 to 150 at markets.

wishIKnew.title: Massage and laundry are cheap
wishIKnew.tip: Thai massage: 200 to 350 baht an hour in local shops, 800 plus in spas. Laundry by weight: 40 to 100 baht a kilo, islands up to 150.

wishIKnew.title: Get a tourist SIM or eSIM
wishIKnew.tip: AIS, True or dtac tourist SIMs cost about 299 to 449 baht for 8 days at airport counters; carrier eSIMs are similar. Bring your passport.

wishIKnew.title: Expect dual pricing
wishIKnew.tip: National parks charge foreigners 200 to 500 baht versus about 40 to 100 for Thais. Budget for it; arguing never works.

wishIKnew.title: Bargain at markets, not malls
wishIKnew.tip: At night markets start near half the first price and smile. Malls, 7-Eleven and food courts are fixed. Blue water machines refill a litre for 1 to 2 baht.

events.name: Sukhothai Loy Krathong and Candle Festival
events.what: The original Loy Krathong: candlelit ruins, fireworks and light and sound shows in the Historical Park.
events.tip: Stay inside the old city so you can walk back late; the light and sound show needs tickets.

events.name: Yi Peng Chiang Saen: Light of Faith on the Mekong
events.what: Lanna lantern nights on the Mekong riverbank at Chiang Saen, quieter than Chiang Mai.
events.tip: Chiang Saen is about 1.5 hours from Chiang Rai town; go by day and stay for dusk.

events.name: Loy Krathong
events.what: Full moon night: everyone floats candlelit krathongs on rivers, lakes and the sea to say thanks.
events.tip: Buy a banana leaf or bread krathong (no foam) from street stalls, about 50 to 100 baht.

events.name: Yi Peng and Loy Krathong, Chiang Mai
events.what: Sky lanterns, glowing old city gates and a krathong parade along the Ping River.
events.tip: Book rooms early; lanterns may only be released at permitted zones, so follow local rules.

events.name: River Kwai Bridge Week and Red Cross Fair
events.what: Nightly light and sound show at the Death Railway bridge, plus a big fair and food stalls.
events.tip: Shows start around 7pm; buy show seats a day ahead and bring mosquito spray.

events.name: Wonderfruit 2026
events.what: Arty, eco minded five day festival of music, talks and wellness at The Fields near Pattaya.
events.tip: About 2 hours from Bangkok; tickets sold only on wonderfruit.co, no refunds or transfers.

events.name: BTS World Tour ARIRANG in Bangkok
events.what: BTS stadium shows at Rajamangala on 3, 5 and 6 December; expect huge crowds around Ramkhamhaeng.
events.tip: Officially sold out; avoid scalpers and take the Airport Rail Link to Ramkhamhaeng.

events.name: Phuket King's Cup Regatta
events.what: Asia's big royal sailing regatta, with yachts racing off Kata and lively shore parties.
events.tip: Watch the starts from Kata Beach or the hill viewpoints; Kata rooms fill fast that week.

events.name: Chiang Mai Design Week 2026
events.what: Citywide design shows, pop up exhibits and makers markets across Chiang Mai's creative districts.
events.tip: Most exhibitions are free; grab the map and cycle between Nimman, Wat Ket and the old city.

events.name: Krabi ReWild Festival
events.what: Eco festival around Krabi's climbing scene: rock climbing, yoga and live music.
events.tip: Dates follow last year's pattern; check before booking and pack climbing shoes if you have them.

events.name: King Bhumibol Memorial Day (Father's Day)
events.what: National holiday honouring the late King Rama IX; yellow flags and ceremonies at government sites.
events.tip: Banks and offices close; tourist spots stay open but Bangkok's Sanam Luang area gets busy.

events.name: Tomorrowland Thailand
events.what: Tomorrowland's first Asian outdoor edition at Wisdom Valley, Pattaya: giant stages, world class DJs.
events.tip: About 2 hours from Bangkok, no camping; 3 day passes sold out fast, check official resale.

events.name: EDC Thailand (December edition)
events.what: Insomniac's neon EDM carnival at Rhythm Park, Laguna Phuket, three nights of big room bass.
events.tip: Strictly 20 plus, bring your passport; hotel bundles include shuttles from Patong and Laguna.

events.name: Chiang Rai Flower Festival
events.what: Cool season blooms, flower tunnels and evening music in Chiang Rai's riverside park.
events.tip: Go late afternoon for golden light; dates follow last season, so confirm with TAT Chiang Rai.

events.name: Bangkok New Year Countdown
events.what: Free riverside fireworks at ICONSIAM plus concerts and drones at CentralWorld and One Bangkok.
events.tip: Take the BTS or a boat early, trains get packed after 10pm; bring water and patience.

events.name: Ao Nang New Year Countdown
events.what: Beach countdown at Ao Nang and Noppharat Thara with DJs, food stalls and midnight fireworks.
events.tip: Book longtail transfers back from Railay before dusk; boats stop early that night.

events.name: New Year's Day holiday
events.what: Nationwide New Year holiday; Thais travel home, so buses, trains and flights fill up.
events.tip: Book transport and island ferries at least two weeks ahead; prices spike over the break.

events.name: Stray Kids World Tour RUN IT in Bangkok
events.what: K pop arena shows at IMPACT Arena, Muang Thong Thani, on Bangkok's northern edge.
events.tip: Listed by aggregators only; confirm on the promoter's page and allow an hour by taxi from central Bangkok.

events.what: Bangkok's Chinatown turns red and gold with lion dances, lanterns and street food crowds.
events.tip: Go early evening by MRT to Wat Mangkon; some Chinese owned shops close for a few days.

events.name: Ayutthaya World Heritage Fair
events.what: Ten nights of light and sound shows, period costume and old Siam food stalls in the Historical Park.
events.tip: The 2026 fair moved to February; confirm 2027 dates before planning. Rent Thai costume for photos.

events.name: Makha Bucha Day
events.what: Buddhist holy day: candlelit wian tian walks around temples; substitute holiday on Monday 22nd.
events.tip: Alcohol sales are banned nationwide on the day and many bars close; plan a temple visit instead.

events.name: Laanta Lanta Festival
events.what: Three day Old Town fest of Chao Leh sea gypsy culture, reggae, food and handicrafts.
events.tip: 2026 ran 27 to 29 March; 2027 dates not yet out, watch Krabi tourism pages.

events.name: Songkran (Thai New Year)
events.what: Nationwide water fight and family homecoming; temples bathe Buddha images, streets become splash zones.
events.tip: Bag your phone in a dry pouch, book transport early, and expect many shops and offices shut.

events.name: S2O Songkran Music Festival

events.what: National holiday with royal portraits, yellow decor and evening ceremonies.
events.tip: Government offices and banks close; dress respectfully near royal ceremonies.

events.what: National holiday honouring Queen Sirikit; blue decor, jasmine garlands and family outings.
events.tip: Long weekend crowds at beach towns near Bangkok; book ahead.

events.name: Half Moon and Jungle parties
events.what: Jungle raves near Ban Tai about a week before and after the full moon.
events.tip: Tickets usually 800 to 1,500 baht; shared taxis wait outside after.

events.name: New Year's Eve, Haad Rin
events.what: Haad Rin's biggest night of the year, one week after the December full moon.
events.tip: Rooms sell out by October; arrive by the 29th.

events.name: Pattaya International Fireworks Festival
events.what: Two nights of international fireworks teams over Pattaya Bay, with free concerts on the beach.
events.tip: Book rooms early and claim a beach spot by late afternoon; rooftop dinners sell out.

events.name: Lopburi Monkey Buffet Festival
events.what: Tables piled with fruit and vegetables for the monkeys at Phra Prang Sam Yot, with costumed dancers.
events.tip: Arrive before 10 am, wear nothing loose and keep your phone strapped.

events.name: Bua Tong bloom, Doi Mae U Kho
events.what: Hillsides of wild yellow Mexican sunflowers in full bloom near Khun Yuam.
events.tip: Go on a weekday morning; it is about 2 hours south of Mae Hong Son town.

events.name: Hua Hin Vintage Car Parade
events.what: Classic cars drive from Bangkok to Hua Hin and gather for a show and parade.
events.tip: Dates are usually announced a few weeks ahead by the Vintage Car Club of Thailand.

events.name: Fly To The Moon, Koh Mak
events.what: A small New Year island music festival on Koh Mak.
events.tip: Book boat and bed together; the island has few rooms over New Year.

events.name: Pattaya Countdown
events.what: New Year's Eve concerts and fireworks on the bay.
events.tip: Roads close near the beach; walk or use baht buses early.

events.name: Wonder One Music Festival
events.what: Thai pop and indie lineup at One Chichan, near Khao Chi Chan south of Pattaya.
events.tip: Book transport back to town in advance; taxis are scarce after the show.

events.name: King Narai Reign Fair
events.what: Lopburi dresses up in Ayutthaya-era costume with light shows at the palace and markets in the old town.
events.tip: Locals wear period dress; costume rental stalls let you join in cheaply.

events.name: Pattaya Music Festival
events.what: Free beach concerts on Friday and Saturday nights through March, with Thai bands on several stages.
events.tip: Stages move between Pattaya Beach, Jomtien and Naklua; check the weekly lineup.

events.name: Poy Sang Long
events.what: Shan novice ordinations: boys dressed as princes carried through town on shoulders, with music and food.
events.tip: Ceremonies differ by temple; ask at Wat Chong Kham or the TAT office for the day of the procession.

events.name: Wan Lai, Pattaya Songkran
events.what: Pattaya's late Songkran: the biggest water fights on Beach Road and in Naklua.
events.tip: Put your phone in a waterproof pouch and expect to be soaked by noon.

events.name: Similan Islands season opening
events.what: The national park reopens for the dive and snorkel season, usually running to mid May.
events.tip: Opening weeks can be rough; for calmer seas and clearer water, go from December.

events.name: Lopburi Monkey Buffet Festival
events.what: The yearly feast for Lopburi's monkeys around Phra Prang Sam Yot.
events.tip: Usually the last Sunday of November; confirm closer to the date.

events.name: Amphawa Floating Market
events.what: Canal market with boat kitchens, from about noon to 9 pm.
events.tip: Come after 3 pm and stay for a firefly boat.

events.name: Amphawa Floating Market
events.what: The busiest day: canal stalls, grilled prawns and live music.
events.tip: Book a homestay early; Saturday rooms go first.

events.name: Amphawa Floating Market
events.what: Canal market with boat kitchens, from about noon to 9 pm.
events.tip: Leave by 8 pm if heading back to Bangkok; the last vans fill fast.

events.name: Cicada Market
events.what: Art and craft night market with live music and a food court.
events.tip: Pair it with Tamarind Market next door for dinner.

events.name: Cicada Market
events.what: Art and craft night market with live music and a food court.
events.tip: Busiest night; get there before 7 pm.

events.name: Cicada Market
events.what: Art and craft night market with live music and a food court.
events.tip: A calmer night than Saturday.

events.name: Pattaya Walking Street
events.what: Neon strip of clubs, bars and go-go bars, closed to traffic each evening.
events.tip: Check drink prices before ordering; adult venues dominate.

events.name: Koh Lipe Walking Street
events.what: Food stalls, shops and cafes along the island's main lane.
events.tip: Eat early in peak season; popular stalls sell out.

events.name: Surin Elephant Round-up
events.what: Surin's famous elephant festival: a buffet for the elephants, parades and stadium shows, with a Red Cross fair.
events.tip: Surin is about 3 hours east of Korat; main shows are on the weekend of 21 and 22 November. Some shows use performing elephants, so choose what you watch with care.

events.name: Red Lotus Sea in bloom
events.what: Talay Bua Daeng turns pink with water lilies; boats run every morning.
events.tip: Be on the water by 6:30 am; flowers close by late morning.

events.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
events.what: Thousands of stalls of clothes, crafts, plants and snacks, about 9 am to 6 pm.
events.tip: Go at 9 am before the heat and crowds.

events.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
events.what: Thousands of stalls of clothes, crafts, plants and snacks, about 9 am to 6 pm.
events.tip: Sunday afternoon is the busiest time of the week.

events.name: Chiang Khan Walking Street
events.what: The riverfront road closes to traffic for snacks, crafts and music each evening.
events.tip: Busiest on cool-season weekends; weekdays are calmer.

events.name: Kad Khuang Mueang Nan
events.what: Walking street market beside Wat Phumin with local food and folk music.
events.tip: Sit on the mats and eat with the locals.

events.name: Kad Khuang Mueang Nan
events.what: Walking street market beside Wat Phumin with local food and folk music.
events.tip: The busiest night of the three.

events.name: Kad Khuang Mueang Nan
events.what: Walking street market beside Wat Phumin with local food and folk music.
events.tip: A calmer evening to finish a weekend in Nan.

events.name: Trang Underwater Wedding
events.what: Couples dive to sign their marriage register underwater near Koh Kradan, part of Trang's Valentine's festival.
events.tip: Rooms on Kradan fill up; book early if you plan to visit that weekend.

events.name: Phanom Rung sunset through the 15 doors
events.what: The setting sun shines straight through all fifteen doorways of the temple.
events.tip: Weather permitting; arrive mid-afternoon to find a spot.

events.name: Thao Suranari Festival
events.what: Korat's biggest festival honouring its heroine, with parades, light and sound shows and a big fair.
events.tip: Evenings around the monument are packed; book rooms early.

events.name: Phanom Rung Festival and sunrise through the 15 doors
events.what: The rising sun lines up through all fifteen doorways, with a festival of processions and light shows at the temple.
events.tip: Sunrise is about 6 am; leave Korat around 3:30 am or stay in Nang Rong near the temple.

events.name: Phi Ta Khon ghost festival
events.what: Dan Sai's masked ghost parade, with huge colourful masks, bells and rockets.
events.tip: Dan Sai is about two hours south of Chiang Khan; dates are set by local mediums a month or two ahead.

events.name: Phanom Rung sunrise through the 15 doors
events.what: The rising sun shines straight through all fifteen doorways.
events.tip: Rainy season: clouds often hide the sun, so keep plans flexible.

events.name: Phanom Rung sunset through the 15 doors
events.what: The setting sun shines through all fifteen doorways.
events.tip: Weather permitting; arrive by mid-afternoon.

events.name: Surin Islands reopen
events.what: Mu Ko Surin National Park reopens to visitors for the dry season.
events.tip: The first weeks can still bring rough seas; check boat operators.

events.name: Tarutao National Park reopens
events.what: Park accommodation and boats to Koh Tarutao restart for the season.
events.tip: Ferries from Pak Bara usually restart around this time too.

events.name: Nan Boat Racing Festival
events.what: Long, carved naga boats race on the Nan River after the end of Buddhist Lent, with crowds and food stalls on the banks.
events.tip: Dates are announced only weeks ahead; ask the TAT Nan office.

events.name: Phimai Festival
events.what: Boat races on the river, a light and sound show at the Khmer temple and a local fair.
events.tip: Book the light and sound show seats in advance.

events.name: Surin Elephant Round-up
events.what: Elephant buffet, parades and stadium shows in Surin, with a Red Cross fair.
events.tip: Surin is about 3 hours from Korat; main shows are expected on the weekend of 20 and 21 November.

events.name: River Kwai Bridge Week
events.what: Light and sound shows at the bridge recall the war years, with a fair and fireworks.
events.tip: Book a seat for the show and a room near the river early.
